results.title: The Top 10 Startups Hiring Right Now, According to LinkedIn - Business Insider
results.content:
The final list showed a few patterns in the types of companies doing well right now. The top three startups on the list, for example, give consumers more control over their purchases and lifestyle, and many offer online accommodations for remote work and invest in employee happiness.

According to LinkedIn, these companies are collectively hiring for more than 3,000 jobs right now, so if you're searching for a career pivot, these top 10 companies could be a good bet. The companies are listed in descending order, with LinkedIn's top rated startup at first place.

## 1. Better.com [...] ## 1. Better.com

What they do: Better.com is a homeownership startup that replaces conventional home-financing with a digitized process eliminating fees, commissions, and unnecessary extra steps for home buyers. They've seen a 200% increase in demand for digitized homeownership projects and funded $8 billion in loans since March.

Who they're hiring: Since March, the company has virtually hired and onboarded over 1,500 employees. As of Monday, Better.com is actively recruiting for leadership development coaches, executive assistants, and employee experience associates.

## 2. DoorDash

What they do: Doordash is a delivery company that has expanded from food services to pharmacy and grocery offerings. The company filed to go public in February [...] ## 4. Samsara

What they do: Samsara is a computer software company that provides AI-based sensor systems. Since March, the company has been focused on creating a smooth transition to remote work, providing leadership training, various events, and iPads for kids to learn remotely.

Who they're hiring: Some actively recruiting positions as of Monday include people data coordinator, business value consultant, and head of product management.

## 5. Databricks

What they do: Databricks is a data and artificial intelligence company that helps organizations make their data ready for analytics so that they can shift their business strategies accordingly. The company was founded in 2013 and has partners including Microsoft and Amazon.

results.title: Startups in Canada That Are Hiring Right Now - Business Insider
results.content:
There are Canadian startups ready to hire Americans right now.

For this list, we curated some of the fast-growing and well-funded startups from Vancouver to Montreal, based on funding data, industry buzz, and a LinkedIn ranking of the Canadian startups on the rise. Business Insider reviewed their job postings and reached out to confirm those companies are open to filling any role with an American worker.

Headquarters: Kitchener, Ontario

What it does: Created by three brothers out of University of Waterloo's startup incubator, ApplyBoard helps international students search and apply for thousands of schools abroad. [...] Headquarters: Toronto, Ontario

What it does: League's app is like an operating system for employee health benefits, helping them manage their care coverage, dependents, and spending accounts at their fingertips.

What you need to know: League has been hiring through the pandemic, and the startup plans to grow by another 150 employees across sales, product, and engineering next year.

"We would certainly consider hiring an American to fill any of those seats," marketing manager Rebecca Orellana said, adding that all employees have the option of working remotely.

Headquarters: Toronto, Ontario

What it does: Next Pathway's software simplifies the process of moving data from legacy data warehouses to the cloud. It completes an end-to-end migration project in 165 days on average. [...] Headquarters: Montreal, Quebec

What it does: Element AI makes tools for enterprise customers that want to build and implement their own artificial intelligence solutions but don't have the technical know-how.

What you need to know: The company's staff shrunk from more than 500 employees to about 350 as it slashed spending during the pandemic. But Element AI is once again growing its team of engineers, product gurus, and IT support technicians as the economy recovers.

"We hire based on competencies and not location," cofounder and chief administrative officer Anne Martel said, adding that US applicants have the option of moving or working remotely.

Headquarters: Toronto, Ontario

results.title: 16 Startups Hiring Techies Now, and the Top Salary Isn’t…
results.content:
Interfere: Founding Designer. NYC, up to $250K. Software that helps teams find broken product experiences and fix them. Founder Luke Shiels started it after one too many afternoons lost to bug hunting. You’d own everything from user interviews to shipped interfaces, which makes you the person who decides what “broken” means.

## For those who like their work to weigh something

Zeno Power: Chief of Staff. Washington, DC, hybrid, up to $200K. Zeno makes nuclear batteries for remote places on Earth, in space and at sea. You’d work next to the CEO on priorities, investor materials and government partnerships. The batteries last for years, and we’re told the meetings don’t. [...] Parallel: basically everything. SF, Palo Alto, NYC, London. Web infrastructure for AI agents. They’re hiring in research, engineering, design, GTM, marketing, finance, legal and ops. If you’ve ever wanted to just send a résumé to a company with no particular role in mind, here’s your chance.

## For the grown-ups in the room

Mixpanel: Director of Product Management. NYC, up to $373K total cash. More than 29,000 companies use its analytics. You’d lead the PMs behind the products that bring in the revenue, which is the job of deciding what everyone else will measure. [...] Here’s this week’s reading from the startup job market, sorted by the kind of person each role is looking for.

## For the people people

Shield AI: Sr. Director, Global People Operations. Seattle, up to $380K. Dallas or San Diego, up to $320K. Same job, $60K apart. That says something about how much location still matters, and that something is “a lot.”

EliseAI: GTM Product Enablement Manager, Housing. NYC or Boston, up to $190K. EliseAI’s agents handle leasing, resident messages and maintenance requests. You’d be the first enablement hire, writing the training, demo scripts and certifications that help the sales team explain the product without saying “it’s basically magic.”

results.title: The Infinite Conflict of Hiring
results.content:
Over my career of founding and investing in hundreds of startups, almost every day I hear Founders complaining about not being able to find the right talent. Not once have I heard a Founder complain about having too many talented people in their startup.

Make it a rule to meet at least one great, talented “candidate” each week, even if you are not recruiting for a relevant role. Don’t lose a great person just to save on 1 or 2 months of salary.

Once you decide you need to hire someone, maybe the biggest mistake founders make is not treating recruiting seriously enough and not putting enough time into it.
